findings.title: Unsanitized feed HTML is stored and rendered as raw HTML
findings.body: PollFeed passes CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) directly to TopicEmbed.import without sanitizing it. TopicEmbed.import creates the post with cook_method raw_html, and Post#cook returns raw verbatim for that method, so feed-supplied markup such as script elements or event-handler attributes becomes the post's cooked HTML and is rendered to forum visitors. A malicious or compromised RSS/Atom feed can therefore achieve stored XSS in users' browsers, including administrators.

findings.title: Embed URL is interpolated unescaped into raw HTML
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import appends "#{url}" to the post body without HTML-escaping or URL-encoding url. Because the resulting post uses raw_html rendering, a feed- or import-supplied URL containing a single quote can break out of the href attribute and inject additional attributes or markup, for example an onclick handler. The URL must be escaped before it is embedded in the generated footer HTML.

findings.title: PollFeed crashes on feed items without a content field
findings.body: The job unconditionally calls i.content.scrub. RSS items commonly provide only description/summary rather than content, in which case i.content is nil and this raises NoMethodError. The exception aborts processing of all remaining items, and because the scheduled job is configured with retry: false, a single such item can prevent every later valid feed entry from being imported on each poll.

findings.title: Embed controller spec expects the old synchronous retriever flow
findings.body: This spec expects TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve to be called, but EmbedController#best now calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: ...). The mocha expectation will therefore fail, and depending on test job settings the enqueued job may also run for real. The spec should expect Jobs.enqueue with :retrieve_topic and the correct arguments instead.

findings.title: TopicEmbed.import has a check-then-create race on embed_url
findings.body: Import first queries TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url) and only creates the embed record if none exists, but concurrent PollFeed and RetrieveTopic jobs (the latter bypasses throttling for staff) can both observe no record for the same new URL and both create a topic/post. The unique database index on embed_url then makes one TopicEmbed.create! raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, failing that job and rolling back its work. The creation path needs to handle the uniqueness conflict or serialize creation per URL.

findings.title: Retrieval throttle key can be left without an expiry
findings.body: retrieved_recently? sets the Redis throttle key with setnx and only afterwards calls expire as a separate command. If the process crashes or Redis errors between the two commands, the key persists forever with no TTL, permanently blocking retrieval for that embed URL and leaving visitors on the loading page. The key should be created atomically with its 60-second expiry.

findings.title: Disqus import now depends on the original site being reachable
findings.body: The import previously created the topic locally from the Disqus export, but now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...), which fetches t[:link] over HTTP. If a thread's link is missing, malformed, or the original article is offline, open() raises or TopicEmbed.import returns nil and that thread's Disqus comments are skipped or the whole import aborts, losing data that is fully present in the export file. The removed --category option also means existing import invocations using it will fail and imported topics can no longer be placed in a category.

findings.title: absolutize_urls mishandles common relative URL forms
findings.body: Only href/src values beginning with '/' are rewritten. Plain relative references such as images/photo.jpg are left relative and will resolve against the Discourse host, producing broken links/images, while protocol-relative references such as //cdn.example.com/photo.jpg are incorrectly rewritten onto the source origin as http://source.example.com//cdn.example.com/photo.jpg. URL resolution should use URI joining against the source URL instead of string prefix checks.

findings.title: Unauthenticated clients can flood retrieval with non-canonical URLs
findings.body: Any client that spoofs the Referer header (the only embeddable-host check is that header, trivially set by non-browser clients) can call embed/best with arbitrary distinct URLs on the embeddable host, and every miss enqueues a RetrieveTopic job. The only throttling is per exact URL string inside the job and TopicEmbed is keyed by the exact URL string, so adding random query parameters, fragments, or other variants of the same article bypasses the throttle, floods the job queue with server-side fetches of the remote host, and can create duplicate topics for the same article. Retrieval needs canonical URL handling and a global/origin rate limit before enqueueing.
